overview:
This wiki explains the subset-intersection network. It is a linear network whose subspace labels come from intersection sizes of three-element subsets, and its target result is that the total number of smaller calls is less than the number of wires times the dimension, written $s<Wm$ in the bit network. The bound says the network makes fewer smaller calls than a naive count of wires times dimension would suggest, and the argument behind it, not the bare count, is what the wiki develops.

The route starts with background. [Linear algebra over a field](linear-algebra.md) supplies vector spaces, linear maps, subspaces and rank. [Fixed-tape machine model](fixed-tape-machine.md) fixes the computational model: a Turing machine with one finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes, where each head moves at most one cell per step.

The second part builds the basic device. [Linear network that restores auxiliary values](linear-network.md) is a fixed network of linear gates that exchanges two banks of values with prescribed signs and returns every auxiliary value to its starting state.

The third part introduces [Frame of a network vertex](frame.md), an invertible linear operator attached to each vertex that changes how the array on each wire is represented. On every route through the network the operator on each role is $D_{\mathrm{sink}}D_{\mathrm{source}}^{-1}$, so only the endpoint frames determine it.

The final part assembles these into the [Subset-intersection network](subset-network.md) and proves the count. It tracks the subspace labels and their rank, showing the total for the bit network is below $Wm$ and the total phase-translation rank for the complex network is strictly below $W_{\rm c}m$.

parts.title: Background and computational model
parts.intro: This part fixes the vocabulary and the machine model used throughout. [Linear algebra over a field](linear-algebra.md) gives the spaces, maps and rank that every later object is built from. [Fixed-tape machine model](fixed-tape-machine.md) states the Turing-machine model whose step costs the network is meant to count.

parts.title: Linear networks that restore values
parts.intro: The main construction starts from a fixed network of linear gates. [Linear network that restores auxiliary values](linear-network.md) shows how banks of values can be exchanged with prescribed signs while every scratch wire returns to its starting state. The later analysis depends on this restoration property.

parts.title: Frames on network vertices
parts.intro: Each vertex of the network carries an invertible operator that changes how the stored array is represented. [Frame of a network vertex](frame.md) defines these operators and shows that on every route the effective operator depends only on the endpoint frames. This reduction is needed to control the rank computations in the final part.

parts.title: Subset-intersection network and its count
parts.intro: This part defines the main object and proves the bound on smaller calls. [Subset-intersection network](subset-network.md) uses the gates and frames from the previous parts, with labels given by intersection sizes of three-element subsets. The proof bounds the total rank of the edge differences for the bit network and the phase-translation factors for the complex network.
